investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested pods because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource label. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted for a remote agent VM stalls indefinitely as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the kata/peer-pods node pool, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which submits a pod that never starts, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever written back to the probe result.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 121s.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=124623, status=fail — the probe timed out waiting for a VM that never started.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence keys were written, confirming the agent creation path never completed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the runner never reaching the VM-ready state.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149919 — independent pod submission also exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=151188 — third independent pod submission also failed identically.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2-node kata/peer-pods pool: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata nodes carry, so even if the kata nodes had free slots the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible.
Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may not have completed on a prior failure).
Lower probability — a recent quota or LimitRange change reduced the number of allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm units on the pool nodes, shrinking available capacity below the concurrent probe demand.

If the kata node pool is genuinely at capacity due to legitimate workloads, coordinate with the infrastructure team to either scale up the kata/peer-pods node pool or increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing nodes.

Review the withCleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure that pods and VMs are reliably cleaned up even when a probe times out or errors, to prevent future slot leakage from eval runs.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 kata nodes, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., API-level agent creation failure before pod submission) would need to be investigated.
If the remote-agent-create probe passed on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling spike rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (i.e., the resource shows as fully available), the root cause would shift to a misconfigured node affinity/selector on the pod spec that prevents scheduling even when capacity exists.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared infrastructure exhaustion cause would be less likely and a check-specific code or configuration issue would be more plausible.
If the eval runner logs showed the pod was never submitted (e.g., an API error before pod creation), the root cause would be upstream of the Kubernetes scheduler.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for a pod scheduling timeout.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that scans for remote-agent pods in Pending or Unknown state older than a configurable TTL and flags them as cleanup failures.

Add a post-run cleanup verification step to the remote-agent eval suite that confirms all probe-created VMs and pods were successfully deleted after each run, catching withCleanup failures before they accumulate.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-15 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never reached the state-polling phase, so zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are fully consumed (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node sets. The pod remained Unschedulable for 147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real inability to provision a remote agent VM, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested pods because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource label. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted for a remote agent VM stalls indefinitely as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the kata/peer-pods node pool, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which submits a pod that never starts, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever written back to the probe result.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 121s.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=124623, status=fail — the probe timed out waiting for a VM that never started.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence keys were written, confirming the agent creation path never completed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the runner never reaching the VM-ready state.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149919 — independent pod submission also exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=151188 — third independent pod submission also failed identically.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, confirming a pod is submitted for a remote VM before any evidence is collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2-node kata/peer-pods pool: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata nodes carry, so even if the kata nodes had free slots the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible.
Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may not have completed on a prior failure).
Lower probability — a recent quota or LimitRange change reduced the number of allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm units on the pool nodes, shrinking available capacity below the concurrent probe demand.

If the remote-agent-create probe passed on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling spike rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (i.e., the resource shows as fully available), the root cause would shift to a misconfigured node affinity/selector on the pod spec that prevents scheduling even when capacity exists.

Preemption was also unavailable on both node sets. The pod remained Unschedulable for 147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real inability to provision a remote agent VM, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so zero evidence was collected and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no preemption victims available and no matching nodes, every remote-agent pod request is immediately Unschedulable. This is a cluster-infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment and is confirmed as an eval-level failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — pod scheduling is the first infrastructure gate that must succeed before any evidence can be collected
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector rules, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized for the expected concurrency, capacity will be exhausted under normal load.

Tertiary — resource leak from a prior eval run: if a previous remote-agent pod was not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs did not complete), it may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that were not released, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event: a node restart, maintenance cordon, or autoscaler scale-down event temporarily reduced kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run. This would be self-resolving but would not explain all three sibling checks failing across a ~5-minute window.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run all three failing remote-agent checks together to confirm shared infrastructure failure

reproductionSteps.details: Query the Kubernetes cluster for the current allocatable and allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on all nodes to determine whether capacity is still exhausted or has recovered.

reproductionSteps.details: List all pods in the remote-agents namespace (or equivalent) to identify any stuck, pending, or running pods that were not cleaned up by a prior eval run's withCleanup handler.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes kata peer-pod VM scheduling layer
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm as the exhausted resource on the 2 nodes eligible for remote-agent pods. All three remote-agent checks fail at this layer before any agent API call is made (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185) are failing with the same class of scheduler error, indicating the entire feature's eval coverage is blocked by the infrastructure constraint.
affectedAreas.details: features.json lines 183-185 register all three checks; degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 mean the feature is at or near outage threshold in the eval system.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe branch
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at lines 1913-1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers the kata peer-pod scheduling path. The probe cannot advance past this call when the scheduler returns Unschedulable.
affectedAreas.details: run-status-probes.mjs lines 1917-1918 show createAgent is the first substantive call after requireOrgId; no evidence can be collected until this succeeds.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266-270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message. All five are missing because the pod never started, making the contract gap a downstream symptom of the scheduling failure rather than an independent defect.
affectedAreas.details: check-expectations.json lines 268-269 define the full required evidence set and the 'hello from aura' message assertion, none of which can be satisfied without a running agent pod.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the Kubernetes cluster for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes — determine current allocatable vs. allocated counts to confirm whether capacity is still depleted.
Audit all currently running or pending remote-agent pods to identify any that were not cleaned up by a prior eval run's withCleanup handler; terminate any leaked pods to free VM slots.

Review the node affinity/selector rules applied to remote-agent pods against the labels on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm whether the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded or represent a labeling drift.

If capacity is confirmed exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the 2 kata-eligible nodes need additional kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity provisioned or whether additional nodes should be labeled to expand the schedulable pool.

After restoring scheduling capacity, re-run all three remote-agent eval checks to confirm recovery and that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are returned with the 'hello from aura' assertion passing.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is still active or has self-resolved. A pass would indicate a transient event; a repeat Unschedulable failure confirms sustained capacity exhaustion.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Matches the reproduction hint supplied in the investigation packet.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node resource allocations
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the 2 kata-eligible nodes have exhausted their VM resource slots. Look for allocatable vs. allocated counts on each node.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query node describe output or resource quota for kata.peerpods.io/vm on all nodes in the cluster.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pending and running remote-agent pods
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether any prior eval run left pods in a non-terminated state that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, which would confirm a resource-leak contributing cause.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Filter by the namespace and labels used by remote-agent pods; look for pods in Pending or Running state that should have been cleaned up.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated eval source paths for recent changes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: infra/evals/status/features.json, infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json, and infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs all have a recent commit (c2e74a6). Reviewing the diff would confirm whether any change to the remote-agent probe logic, node affinity configuration, or resource requests was introduced.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty, so c2e74a6 is a hypothesis only — the diff must be reviewed before attributing causality.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agent sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared Unschedulable failure pattern persists across all three checks in a fresh run, strengthening the shared-infrastructure diagnosis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unallocated on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission control issue would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and returns all required evidence, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief node event or autoscaler action) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules are confirmed correct, the root cause would shift to a node labeling or affinity configuration drift rather than capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the failure would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared infrastructure constraint — but the supplied evidence shows all three siblings failing (sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

If a prior eval run's cleanup handler (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) is confirmed to have completed successfully and released all VM slots, a resource leak from the eval runner would be ruled out as a contributing cause.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm node resource availability (allocatable minus allocated) and alerts before full exhaustion, providing earlier warning before pod scheduling fails.

Add a pre-flight eval check that verifies at least one node satisfying the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules has available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting agent creation, allowing faster failure with a more actionable message.

Add a cleanup-verification eval step that confirms no remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are left in a non-terminated state after each run cycle, catching resource leaks from withCleanup failures.

Consider adding a historical baseline to the remote-agent eval checks (verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null) so that regressions from a known-passing state can be detected and the currentlyRegressedFromPass flag can be used in triage.
